summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with experience in high-performance and parallel computing: CUDA kernel optimization, MPI distributed systems, and SLURM-managed cluster workloads. Strong background in memory coalescing, load balancing, and performance benchmarking, backed by hands-on work engineering large-scale data pipelines and memory management for volumetric datasets.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered a custom data pipeline for the BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI dataset with batch-loading memory management for large-scale 3D volumetric inputs.
Led a cross-cultural team of 7 as the sole technically-experienced student, restructuring task distribution to deliver the full pipeline within a 6-week window.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU TorchScript), a ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.
Achieved 1.5-2x speedup in convolution operations through efficient global memory utilization.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Implemented distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers with synchronous soma updates on a SLURM-managed cluster.
Achieved up to 10.49x speedup with 12 slave processes; characterized scaling behavior across dendrite counts and compartment depths.
Identified load imbalance effects showing up to 65% performance degradation under uneven work distribution.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000x5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
Achieved up to 30x speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); showed dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC with <1% accuracy degradation, near-lossless compression.
